transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-08 15:00 PST
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Ana Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ethan Navarro (BlueMarlin), Priya Singh (BlueMarlin), Marcus Holt (BlueMarlin), Daniel Kwon (BlueMarlin)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and BlueMarlin to understand channel/reseller intent, technical constraints for a GPU-onramp in BlueMarlin's VPC offering, security/compliance requirements, and to scope an initial benchmark/pilot. Focus on routing, multi-tenant isolation, and pilot timeline.

Topics Covered:
- Partnership model: reseller vs ISV embed vs co-sell
- Technical onramp: VPC peering, private deployment, or dedicated pools
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
- Performance: latency targets, quantization tradeoffs, kernel selection
- Commercial: reserved capacity vs usage pricing, margins for partner

Key Action Items (captured in notes as well): Maya to send doc + pricing; Jordan to draft benchmark plan; BlueMarlin to share fleet spec.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya, AE on Redwood partner program. Jordan and Ana from SE team. Ethan?
[00:18] Ethan Navarro: Yeah hi, Ethan here — head of cloud partnerships at BlueMarlin. Thanks for making time, we've been looking at ways to add an LLM inference onramp for our managed GPU offering.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: Nice to meet you all. High level, Redwood provides hosted, dedicated and private deployment. For partners like you we often do a VPC/on-prem package or dedicated pools that sit behind partner control plane.
[00:46] Priya Singh: When you say "sit behind" can you clarify — are we talking peering into Redwood's infra or a customer-managed control plane? We have strict tenancy, can't have shared data leakage.
[01:05] Ana Ruiz: Right — good question. There's multiple patterns. Hosted API with VPC egress, or we can deploy Private in your VPC (single-tenant control plane). We also offer Dedicated reserved GPU pools where compute is isolated per partner. There are tradeoffs — dedicated gives stronger isolation but higher baseline cost.
[01:30] Marcus Holt: Security is big for us. We need to understand KMS integration and whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys, key rotation, and audit logs. Also SOC2 evidence and ISO stuff.
[01:48] Maya Patel: Absolutely — we have SOC2 Type II, ISO90... uh sorry that was wrong — ISO 27001, and our private plane supports KMS integrations — you can bring your own KMS or use cloud provider KMS; HSM support via partner integrations, we can share the security pack after this call.
[02:10] Daniel Kwon: Quick commercial question: are we expected to resell Redwood or act as a reseller and host the model? What's typical?
[02:24] Maya Patel: Partners do both. Two common models: reseller (you resell Redwood hosted or Dedicated instances and take margin) or co-managed private deployment where you host the runtime in your VPC and we do support/updates. The co-managed gives you control for data residency.
[02:42] Ethan Navarro: Our preference is co-managed in the short term — we want to provision in our customers' VPCs. But we need a fast onramp for smaller accounts where we can't provision dedicated infra. So hybrid: hosted for small, VPC/private for larger.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: That's a common pattern. Technically that maps to: Redwood-hosted with route-based fallback and a private deployment for anchor customers. We can add smart routing so calls go to partner VPC when capacity exists, else fall back to hosted. That preserves latency SLOs and partner control.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Latency is critical — sub 150ms p95 for chat use cases. How does continuous batching and kv cache affect tail latency in your runtime?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: Batching reduces cost but can increase p95 if we wait for batch windows. We have workload-aware batching that adapts, with fast-path for urgent (low-latency) requests. Also prefix/KV caching helps a lot for chat — we can keep KV in memory on the same GPU instance to reduce per-token work. But quantization choices and kernel selection matter — we'll need to pick a model variant optimized for your sequence lengths.
[04:05] Marcus Holt: And for on-prem or VPC deployment, can we enforce BYOK (bring-your-own-key) and keep logs within our logging stack?
[04:16] Ana Ruiz: Yes — Private deploys support BYOK and ship audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. We have a log-forwarder and can integrate with Splunk/Datadog. There are some caveats around performance telemetry if you restrict outbound to 0 — we'll clarify what telemetry we need for support.
[04:36] Ethan Navarro: For the benchmark/pilot, what metrics should we be measuring? We want realistic cost modeling to set pricing tiers.
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Typical metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency per seq len, cost per 1k tokens (with and without KV cache), throughput at target concurrency, and memory footprint across GPUs. We'll provide scripts to drive inference and collect those metrics.
[05:05] Priya Singh: Any dependencies on particular GPU types? We run a mixed fleet — A100s and some newer H100s in a few regions.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: We support both; kernel selection differs. H100 gives better perf for certain transformer kernels but cost tradeoffs apply. Also, quantization profiles differ — 4-bit quantization on A100 can work but H100 often gives better headroom. We'll propose model variants per hardware.
[05:36] Daniel Kwon: Curious on the economics — can Redwood do reserved capacity for channel partners with commit discounts? We need predictable margin.
[05:47] Maya Patel: Yes, Dedicated reserved pools can be sold with commit tiers; we have partner pricing that allows you to resell with margin. We'll send an indicative partner price sheet.
[06:00] Ethan Navarro: Good. On the security docs, we often need a partner ATO package. Can you include network diagrams, data flow, and the KMS workflow?
[06:12] Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll include an architecture diagram and the KMS flow. Also note we can provide a minimal onramp template for your engineering team to speed up VPC deployment.
[06:24] Marcus Holt: A practical thing — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning? We need RBAC and user audit trails.
[06:33] Ana Ruiz: Yes SAML SSO is supported; SCIM for provisioning on Private is available. RBAC with per-route permissions and token-scoped keys is how we recommend for partners.
[06:50] [crosstalk] Ethan Navarro: When you say per-route, is that at the model endpoint level?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: Correct — you can scope tokens to specific models and rate limits.
[07:05] Priya Singh: For the pilot timeline — assuming we sign off quickly, how fast can Redwood spin up a private deployment in our VPC? We have an aggressive timeline (end of year).
[07:18] Ana Ruiz: Typical private deploy with automation can be done in 2–4 weeks once we have network access and KMS details; dedicated GPU pools a bit longer if we need provisioned hardware in your DC. Hosted fallback can be immediate for small customers.
[07:35] Daniel Kwon: Ok that aligns with our expectations. One more constraint: some customers require data not leave EU. Are you able to restrict regions and data residency?
[07:45] Maya Patel: Yes, region pinning and data residency policies are supported. Private deployments of course keep data in-region. For hosted we have region-specific endpoints and can exclude failovers outside region.
[07:58] Ethan Navarro: Let's talk about instrumentation — for our billing model we need token-level metering and cost attribution per tenant. Is that supported?
[08:09] Jordan Lee: Yes we provide token-level metering with per-token attribution and can push usage to your billing system via webhooks or you can pull via API. There is also an accounting export for reserved capacity allocations.
[08:24] Marcus Holt: What's the failure mode if a model variant is slower or incompatible — do you have automatic fallbacks?
[08:33] Ana Ruiz: Yes automatic fallback policies exist — e.g., if a quantized model errors or is too slow, router can route to a compatible variant in another pool or region. There are failover rules that keep service up but we can configure per-partner.
[08:48] [silence 10s]
[09:00] Jordan Lee: I want to flag a potential gotcha: telemetry needs a small egress for health pings. If you have strict per-customer outbound rules, we can run an internal agent mode but that adds ops overhead.
[09:16] Priya Singh: Ok we'll review with infra.
[09:22] Ethan Navarro: On benchmarks — can you run a sample with our 3-shot prompts and 512 token sequences? Those are common with our customers.
[09:33] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include those in the benchmark script. Also will vary sequence lengths to show p95 shifts.
[09:46] Daniel Kwon: Any partners you've onboarded with similar reseller expectations? A-Compute was mentioned in our eval — how are we different?
[09:57] Maya Patel: We aim for predictable inference economics and strong tooling for rollouts — traffic split, canary, auto fallback. Competitors may focus on model access but not the runtime ops we provide. We'll send case studies — e.g., a recent telco rollout where we reduced per-token cost 28%.
[10:15] Marcus Holt: Ok, security doc please. Also we need a contact for SOC evidence.
[10:23] Maya Patel: I'll send our security pack and put you in touch with our compliance lead.
[10:30] Ethan Navarro: How about commercial model — do we need an MSA or is there a partner program agreement?
[10:39] Maya Patel: There's a partner addendum to our MSA; for early pilots we can do an LOI and then move to full partner agreement. I'll share the partner program deck.
[10:52] Priya Singh: For the technical POC, can we get a 2-hour window where Redwood runs the benchmark in our env and we watch? Would prefer that than handing over secrets at first.
[11:04] Jordan Lee: Yes we can do a joint-run benchmark. We'll prepare scripts and can run them with live telemetry; you'll see logs and results.
[11:15] Ethan Navarro: Perfect. Timeline wise, we'll aim to confirm pilot scope by Nov 12.
[11:22] Maya Patel: Noted — we'll target Nov 12 for scope sign-off and propose specific slots for the benchmark week of Nov 16.
[11:30] [short pause]
[11:45] Ana Ruiz: Quick technical note: for mixed fleet we'll recommend model variants mapped to GPU type to avoid double quantization. We'll include mapping in the benchmark plan.
[12:00] Daniel Kwon: Is there any special networking required for private deploy — like BGP or VPN?
[12:10] Ana Ruiz: We support both cross-account VPC peering and site-to-site VPN. For lower latency we recommend peering; for air-gapped customers VPN can be used. We'll send a network diagram for both patterns.
[12:30] Marcus Holt: Good. One last nit: do you produce per-route SLA documents? Our procurement will ask for SLA details.
[12:40] Maya Patel: Yes we have SLA tiers for Dedicated and enterprise Private. Hosted has best-effort SLOs but enterprise adds SLA. We'll include the SLA excerpt in the partner packet.
[12:55] Ethan Navarro: Anything else on your side?
[13:00] Jordan Lee: No — just to confirm we'll need your fleet inventory and a list of 2–3 tenant use-cases to model in the benchmark.
[13:10] Priya Singh: We'll get that.
[13:14] Maya Patel: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send security docs, partner deck, and pricing. Jordan will send benchmark plan. BlueMarlin will send fleet spec and confirm pilot date.
[13:29] Daniel Kwon: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
